title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Settling Export Records That Run on a Merged Clock
content:
## Subject

This page covers how a Demurrage and Detention Free Time export record, whose demurrage and detention share one merged clock, is taken through to settlement after its last clock has stopped. It describes what each part of that close-out is and who performs it. Any given part comes into play only where the policy that governs it provides for it, and the close-out is complete when the record stands settled with nothing owed on it.

## Parts performed by the desk

**Goodwill on demurrage.** Its size is taken from the demurrage line as invoiced; it is recorded against that line's invoice reference, which is the reference returned when the line is booked; and the time allowed for asking for it is counted from that line's invoice date.

**Settlement.** A record is closed as settled when payments, waivers and credits have brought what it owes to nothing.

**Invoice lines.** Detention and demurrage are each priced from the dates the terminal and depot recorded and from the product on the record, under the rules for the line concerned. On the merged clock of an export record the two kinds of chargeable day belong to a single run, the detention days reaching up to the full gate-in and the demurrage days lying beyond it, and the demurrage days take their slab positions from the chargeable days entered on the record's detention line.

## Part performed by the billed party

**Card payment.** Paying the balance is the billed party's own act, done by card by the customer themselves; it is a payment, not a confirmation that the desk seeks. A payment can never be larger than what the record owes at the moment it is taken, and in a close-out of this kind it is meant to leave the record owing nothing.

## Timing

No part hangs on something happening elsewhere or on days going by. Every part is a desk booking completed on the spot, or else the customer paying by card while still in the same contact.
